Colorado: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open Colorado on the map

Key dates

  • Mail ballots sent to every active registered voter: October 2, 2026 to October 9, 2026. Colorado mails a ballot to every active voter, so you do not need to request one. If you return it by mail, the Secretary of State advises mailing it by October 26. After that, use a drop box or voter center. Ballots must arrive by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.
  • In-person voting at voter service and polling centers: October 19, 2026 to November 3, 2026. Counties had to open their required voter centers by October 19. Hours and locations vary by county, so check GoVoteColorado.gov.
  • Deadline to register or update registration online or by mail and still be mailed a ballot: October 26, 2026. After October 26, eligible Coloradans can still register and vote in person at a voter service and polling center until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Voter centers are open 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Ballots must be received at a drop box, voter center or county clerk by 7:00 p.m.

Official election information: vote.gov

Who's running

Only the U.S. Senate and governor races are loaded so far. Other statewide offices, ballot measures, U.S. House and local races aren't loaded yet. Check your sample ballot for the full list.

State

Governor and Lieutenant Governor

Voters elect a governor and lieutenant governor together on one ticket for a four-year term. This is an open seat because Gov. Jared Polis (D) is term-limited. The running mates are: Weiser with Lesley Dahlkemper, Marx with George Washington Markert, Hamilton with James K Treibert, Mulder with Wayne Harlos, Peckman with T.J. Cole, Underwood with Frank Atwood, and Lopez with Taralyn Romero.
